selection.year_semantics: CVE identifier year, not disclosure or fix year
selection.score_policy: Keep the scoring source for every metric; a case qualifies when NVD, a CVE CNA, a national CSIRT, or an official distribution advisory publishes a CVSS v3.x score of at least 7.0. Preserve material source disagreements instead of silently choosing one.

metric_source_urls.official distribution or CSIRT advisory: Use the case's severity_source_url or severity_source_urls.

taxonomy.name: Common Weakness Enumeration
taxonomy.mapping_policy: Primary CWE is curated from the fixed root cause and invariant. source_reported_cwe preserves the CVE record's mapping when present; related_cwes records a contributing cause or consequence.

runtime_boundary: All 20 entries are active deterministic rules in --use-cve-rules, which remains opt-in and disabled by default. Each rule is derived from a manually reviewed CVE fix, has a pre-fix signature and fixed-control fixture, and is grouped under a curated primary CWE. Fixture replay validates the encoded signature and narrow safe filter; it does not establish scanner recall across Linux. Current full-tree validation scanned 2,791 C/H files, parsed 2,786, reported five parser gaps, and found 21 locations (9 exact-safe filtered, 12 retained in 3 rule families). Ten rules had no matching location. CVE-2025-38193 remains a plausible resource-impact candidate, not a confirmed new CVE; CVE-2022-0847 has one conservatively retained, manually reviewed safe implementation candidate. No new PoC was run for the 17 additional CVEs.

activation_validation.limitations: The fixtures are focused function snippets derived from verified fixes, not full historical source-tree replays for every CVE. C lexical parsing does not prove semantics, macro expansion, Kconfig behavior, or general data flow. A no-match result is not evidence of safety.

cases.root_cause: An on-disk EA name_len can exceed the bytes occupied by its enclosing EA entry; ntfs_list_ea then reads or accounts for bytes outside that entry.
cases.trigger_condition: Mount a crafted NTFS image and enumerate extended attributes whose name_len exceeds the decoded EA entry size.
cases.fixed_invariant: Before reading the name or updating output size, require name_len <= the same enclosing EA entry size.

groups.name: Improper Validation of Specified Quantity in Input

cases.root_cause: A disk-supplied nonresident attribute alloc_size lacked a volume-size sanity bound, allowing later metadata and cluster accounting to trust an impossible extent.
cases.trigger_condition: Mount a crafted NTFS image with a non-sparse nonresident attribute whose alloc_size is larger than the volume.
cases.fixed_invariant: Bound alloc_size before accepting applicable attributes; preserve the sparse/compressed first-segment exception, which may legitimately exceed volume size and needs its own format-consistency checks.

cases.root_cause: The configured perturb period was not range-checked before multiplication by HZ, so negative or excessive values could overflow or become invalid timer periods and expose a race.
cases.trigger_condition: Configure SFQ with a negative or excessively large perturb period.
cases.fixed_invariant: Before multiplying by HZ, reject negative values and values above INT_MAX / HZ. Zero is valid and disables the perturb timer.

rule_validation.pre_fix_replay: The parent of mainline fix 7ca52541c05c832d32b112274f81a985101f9ba8 parsed 1/1 sch_sfq.c and retained its unbounded conversion.
rule_validation.current_scope_scan: net/sched parsed 81/81 C/H files; 2 structural hits, 1 exact fixed-SFQ hit filtered, 1 cls_flow review bundle retained.

runtime.environment: QEMU/KVM, 1 vCPU, 256 MiB RAM, no virtual NIC
runtime.counterfactual_guard_result: A temporary INT_MAX/HZ check rejected the same high input with EINVAL.

rule_validation.assessment: Plausible aggregate CPU-impact candidate, not a confirmed vulnerability. Unprivileged user-namespace reachability, native-host impact, other HZ values, and the 64-bit wrap-to-short-period case remain untested.

cases.root_cause: The ARP rewrite wrote through skb_store_bits without first making the exact range writable; a splice-imported fragment could still reference a read-only file page, which was modified in place.
cases.trigger_condition: Exercise the ebt_snat ARP rewrite on a non-linear skb containing a splice-imported file page.
cases.fixed_invariant: Make the full ARP sender hardware address range private and writable before reading or writing it.

cases.component: OverlayFS copy-up and id-mapped ownership handling
cases.root_cause: Copying a capable setuid file from a nosuid mount across OverlayFS ownership mappings could assign or preserve ownership and privilege metadata incorrectly.
cases.trigger_condition: A local user copies a capable file from a nosuid lower mount into an OverlayFS mount with the relevant uid mapping.
cases.fixed_invariant: Copy-up must preserve the lower/upper mount ownership and privilege semantics; a capability-bearing file must not gain executable privilege across an invalid id mapping.

groups.name: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization (Race Condition)

cases.root_cause: Concurrent device reconfiguration could change hard_header_len between separate reads used for skb reserve, allocation, and construction; a larger earlier reserve then moved skb data before its allocation.
cases.trigger_condition: Race a packet socket send with a network-device type or header-length reconfiguration.
cases.fixed_invariant: Take one allocation-time header-length snapshot and use it consistently for reserve and construction, including retry paths.

cases.root_cause: Positive drop-error verdicts were accepted; an error value resembling NF_ACCEPT could make the netfilter hook path free the same skb twice.
cases.trigger_condition: Install an nftables verdict with a positive drop error that is interpreted as accept by a later hook path.
cases.fixed_invariant: Reject invalid positive drop errors and preserve exactly one skb owner on every hook verdict path.

cases.root_cause: Concurrent xenwatch backend-change notifications could call xen_9pfs_front_free twice for the same front-end state.
cases.trigger_condition: Race multiple backend state-change notifications during Xen 9p front-end teardown.
cases.fixed_invariant: Serialize teardown so only one caller releases the front-end state; subsequent callers must observe the completed teardown.

cases.root_cause: A race in io_uring timeout completion and cancellation could release a request while another path still used it.
cases.trigger_condition: Race timeout cancellation, completion, and request cleanup through io_uring.
cases.fixed_invariant: Keep the timeout request alive until all completion and cancellation users have dropped their references.

cases.root_cause: An incorrect NFT_STATEFUL_EXPR check allowed an nftables transaction path to retain inconsistent object state and later use an already-freed object.
cases.trigger_condition: A local user with the required namespace capability submits a crafted nftables stateful-expression transaction.
cases.fixed_invariant: Validate expression/object state consistently before transaction commit and keep referenced objects alive through all transaction users.

cases.root_cause: io_msg_ring called io_fput_file for a fixed file and dropped a reference owned by the registered ring, permitting use after free.
cases.trigger_condition: Invoke io_msg_ring with a fixed file while another path uses the registered file reference.
cases.fixed_invariant: Do not release the persistent fixed-file reference as if it were a transient file reference.

cases.root_cause: Anonymous sets were mishandled across a batch transaction, allowing a set to be freed while another transaction operation still referenced it.
cases.trigger_condition: Submit crafted nftables batch operations involving anonymous sets with the required CAP_NET_ADMIN in the network namespace.
cases.fixed_invariant: Defer reclamation until batch operations and all references to the anonymous set have completed.

cases.root_cause: After forwarding transferred skb ownership, an error return still changed the result to SHOT, causing the core to drop an skb no longer owned by the action path.
cases.trigger_condition: Take an error path after tcf_mirred_forward has consumed or transferred the skb.
cases.fixed_invariant: Only request a core drop while the action still owns the skb; never dereference or free it after ownership transfer.

cases.root_cause: Under concurrency, a tree connection could be freed on disconnect while another path still held and later dereferenced its pointer.
cases.trigger_condition: Race tree-connect disconnect and concurrent SMB request paths that retain the tcon.
cases.fixed_invariant: Hold a valid tcon reference across every concurrent user and free only after the final reference is released.

cases.root_cause: A delayed fuse_release_end could call iput after a submount superblock was destroyed; the per-connection wait counter did not cover each submount superblock.
cases.trigger_condition: Unmount a virtiofs submount while release requests are still completing asynchronously.
cases.fixed_invariant: Complete relevant release requests before shutting down each superblock; a connection-wide wait count is not a substitute for per-superblock lifetime ordering.

groups.name: Improper Control of a Resource Through its Lifetime

cases.root_cause: GSO removed the skb destructor but retained the socket reference, leaving skb ownership and socket lifetime inconsistent when the original skb was later orphaned.
cases.trigger_condition: Use a UDP GSO skb through the Open vSwitch userspace-then-output path, then orphan the original skb after its destructor was removed.
cases.fixed_invariant: Transfer or drop skb destructor and socket ownership together; the skb must not retain a socket reference after the matching ownership mechanism is removed.

cases.root_cause: New pipe_buffer flags were not initialized on two paths, so stale PIPE_BUF_FLAG_CAN_MERGE state could authorize writes into read-only page-cache files.
cases.trigger_condition: An unprivileged local user primes a pipe and uses splice plus write to reach a page-cache-backed read-only file page.
cases.fixed_invariant: Initialize every pipe_buffer flag field on every construction path; merge permission must not be inherited from stale storage.

rule_validation.manual_review: anon_pipe_write explicitly assigns packet or merge flags on the mutex-protected path; the filter did not prove this full path safe and conservatively retained it. A model-review attempt was blocked by the platform security review; no PoC was run.

cases.root_cause: Incorrect VLAN-header arithmetic underflowed or overstated a copy length, allowing the nft payload path to copy beyond its stack scratch buffer.
cases.trigger_condition: With the required network capability, evaluate a crafted nft payload expression against VLAN-tagged packet data at boundary-crossing offsets and lengths.
cases.fixed_invariant: Derive the remaining copy length with checked arithmetic that accounts for VLAN header bytes exactly once and keeps every copy within its destination.

source_reported_cwe: Out-of-bounds Write (text mapping; no CWE ID)
cases.root_cause: The kTLS splice path appended pages to the sk_msg scatterlist without updating its copybreak/current cursor, so a later copy could reuse stale scatterlist position state.
cases.trigger_condition: Splice data into a kTLS socket and then take a send/copy path that appends to the same sk_msg scatterlist.
cases.fixed_invariant: After adding splice pages, synchronize copybreak and the current scatterlist cursor with the new end before another path appends data.

cases.root_cause: The paged allocation path omitted fraggap from linear alloclen while the subsequent copy still wrote those bytes into the linear area.
cases.trigger_condition: Build a fragmented IPv4 packet that takes the paged allocation path with a nonzero fraggap.
cases.fixed_invariant: Allocation and paged lengths must account for fraggap consistently with the bytes copied into each skb region.
